title: Why is it thirty whichever way we multiply two, three and five?
description: A block of small cubes is counted three ways: by its front, by its side and by its top. Every count gives thirty, so the order of multiplying does not matter. Keeko doubts this and says another order changes the total.
teaching_notes: One idea: the same block of cubes gives the same total however we group the counting, so the order of multiplying does not change the product. Watch for students who think a different order gives a different total.

source: Using this diagram, can you explain why 30 = 2 × 3 × 5, no m
video_script.why: The child sees with a block of cubes that two, three and five multiply to thirty in whatever order they are taken.
video_script.substitution: the book's own block of cubes, with three cubes along the width, two along the height and five along the depth
video_script.anchor: the block of small cubes of the book, three wide, two high and five deep
video_script.wrong_answer: multiplying in another order changes the total
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks that taking the numbers in another order gives a different number of cubes.
video_script.payoff_line: It is the same block of cubes, so the total is thirty in any order

final_answer.value: 30 = 2 × 3 × 5 in any order, because it is the same block of cubes
final_answer.spoken: thirty in any order, because it is the same block of cubes

maths_rules: the block has 3 cubes along the width, 2 along the height and 5 along the depth
front: 3 × 2 = 6 cubes in a layer, 5 layers, 6 × 5 = 30
side: 2 × 5 = 10 cubes in a slice, 3 slices, 10 × 3 = 30
top: 3 × 5 = 15 cubes in a layer, 2 layers, 15 × 2 = 30
the block is the same each time, so 2 × 3 × 5 = 3 × 2 × 5 = 5 × 2 × 3 = 30
video_script.design: One block of cubes stands on the board. It is cut into layers three ways, and each cut is counted.
open_questions: The book's picture is not in the extracted text; the block of three by two by five cubes follows the worklist description. Check it against the printed picture.
